terms.comment: From lēvis, smooth; classical in the sense “smooth”. No source gives an ironing board.
Morgan–Owens: an iron is simply ferrum.

evidence: Mart. 2.46.3: tua collūcent prēla lacernīs (Lewis & Short)

sources: Lewis & Short: premo · Lewis & Short: levigo · Lewis & Short: prelum

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. laundry (place to wash clothes), laundry: do the laundry, iron (clothes), soap: laundry detergent, laundry: dry cleaner’s. John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, supplied PDF (printed page numbers): pp. 38, 123, 124, 303, 307, 317, 334, 338, 404.
Cicero from the Latinitas loci collection; Laberius and Martial as cited by L&S.
The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 334.
